panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Clinical photograph of a neonate showing cicatricial lesions over both thighs and groin in an L1-L4 dermatomal distribution, a classic CVS manifestation; no exclusion. B: Close-up clinical photograph of the left thigh with cicatricial scarring in an L5 dermatomal distribution, consistent with CVS. C: Clinical photograph of the lower back with extensive cicatricial lesions in an L5 dermatomal distribution, consistent with CVS. D: Clinical photograph showing healed cicatricial lesions over thighs and groin on DOL 4, consistent with CVS. E: Clinical photograph showing linear cicatricial scarring on the anterior left thigh, consistent with CVS cicatricial skin lesions. F: Clinical photograph showing a hypopigmented cicatricial lesion on the lateral right thigh, consistent with CVS cicatricial skin lesion.

panels.figure_caption: Serial clinical photographs of the neonate showing cicatricial rash over both thighs, groin, and lower back. Panels A-C were taken on DOL 1, and panels D-F were taken on DOL 4. (A) Cicatricial lesions over both thighs and groin on DOL 1, corresponding to the L1-L4 lumbar dermatomes. (B) Cicatricial scarring over the lateral aspect of the left thigh, corresponding to the L5 dermatome. (C) Extensive cicatricial lesions involving the lower back, corresponding to the L5 dermatome. (D) Healed cicatricial lesions over the thighs and groin on DOL 4. (E) Linear cicatricial scarring over the anterior aspect of the left thigh. (F) Hypopigmented cicatricial lesion over the lateral aspect of the right thigh. DOL: day of life
in_text_mentions: On admission, the baby was hypoxic (SpO2 78%) with mild tachypnea (respiratory rate 64/min) and tachycardia (heart rate 160/min). Physical examination revealed mild subcostal and intercostal retractions, hypotonia, lethargy, and moderate encephalopathy as per modified Sarnat and Sarnat staging [5]. A cicatricial rash was noted over both thighs, groin, and lower back, involving the L1-L5 lumbar dermatomes (Figure 1).
